name: PDO nose thread lift
lead: A PDO nose thread lift is a minimally invasive, non-surgical rhinoplasty procedure in which absorbable polydioxanone (PDO) threads are inserted under the skin of the nose, sometimes together with filler, to raise the bridge or lift the tip. People choose it for a straighter, higher-looking bridge or a more defined tip without an operation.[1]

A 2024 review in Skin Research and Technology describes using absorbable 'volumizing' threads, mostly PDO and often barbed, with fillers: longer threads support the bridge and shorter ones lift the tip. Because the threads supply structural support, the authors say less filler is needed, which lowers the risk of an overly wide nose, and the combination allows more precise contouring than filler alone.[1][3]

The published literature is small: the 2024 case-based review and one registered pilot trial of 10 participants.[1][2] The related thread-lift technique for facial sagging is described as working by prompting collagen production as the threads dissolve over about six months.[4]
infobox: About six months, two to three times (authors' experience)

paras: A 2024 review describes non-surgical rhinoplasty using absorbable 'volumizing threads' combined with fillers, and explores whether this gives more precise nasal contouring than filler alone.[1] Longer threads are used along the bridge and shorter ones for tip lift; the authors say the technique may last longer than filler alone.[3]

Non-surgical rhinoplasty more generally uses injectable fillers, usually hyaluronic acid or calcium hydroxyapatite, to raise a flat bridge, lift a drooping tip or smooth bumps. Wikipedia notes that because fillers add volume they cannot reduce nose size, although a straighter-looking nose can appear smaller.[5]

PDO threads provide mechanical support under the skin and are absorbed over time. In facial thread lifts, PDO threads are reported to dissolve in about six months while prompting fibroblasts to produce collagen.[4] In the nose, the review describes threads as a scaffold that lifts the bridge or tip and reduces the filler volume required.[3]

The 2024 review examines adverse effects through clinical cases. Threads placed too shallowly can be visible, palpable or protrude through skin; threads along the columella can emerge inside the mouth; off-midline threads can irritate the inner nasal lining; and stretching the philtrum soon after treatment may move threads.[3]

Infection is described as rare and linked mainly to poor sterile technique, retained protruding threads or prior implants, with the nasal tip at higher risk. Dimpling is uncommon, granuloma formation is rare and mainly seen after prior nasal surgery, and tissue necrosis or blindness are described as rare complications when threads are combined with fillers.[3]

The review's prevention advice includes placing threads in the correct plane, checking the inside of the mouth after the procedure, strict aseptic technique, caution with prior implants, prompt removal of exposed threads, and limiting repeat treatments because excessive procedures can cause fibrosis.[3] For filler-based nose reshaping generally, Wikipedia identifies vascular occlusion as the most serious risk.[5]

A small registered trial of non-surgical rhinoplasty with PDO threads (n=10) was completed in 2021; results are not published in the registry entry.[2] The main published source is the 2024 case-based review, which presents individual illustrative cases rather than before-and-after measurements or patient totals.[1][3]

card.summary: Absorbable threads placed in the nose to lift bridge or tip without surgery; very little published evidence.
card.aka: Nose thread lift, non-surgical rhinoplasty with threads
card.note: Evidence is one case-based review and a 10-person registered trial.

quick.overview:
PDO nose threads are dissolvable threads inserted into the nose, sometimes with filler, as a non-surgical way to change bridge or tip shape.

The published evidence is thin.
quick.mechanism: Absorbable polydioxanone threads are placed under the skin to add support and volume.
quick.risks: A 2024 review discusses adverse effects of nose thread procedures and prevention methods; details of their frequency were not reviewed here.

chain: Absorbable PDO threads are placed under the nasal skin
Threads support the bridge or lift the tip, often with filler
Straighter, higher bridge or more defined tip without surgery
angle.text: Threads give the nose structural lift: longer ones support the bridge and shorter ones raise the tip, so the profile looks straighter or more defined. The effect is temporary because PDO is absorbed.
